title: test(idd-doctor,advisory-convergence): cover two gate-integrity call sites, not just their extracted helpers
body:
## Background

A 2026-08-02 re-audit of roadmap #1712 (`Roadmap: close the fail-open
and livelock seams in the autonomous gate chain`) checked all nine
tracked fixes for a specific regression-test shape: an extracted
helper function gets direct unit tests, but the call site that
actually consumes the helper's return value in the real production
code path stays untested -- so a revert of the call site's own
defensive check back to its pre-fix, fail-open behavior leaves the
full test suite green. #1691 (PR#1759, `readCleanupEvidenceTrustedLogins`
in `idd-doctor.mts`) already showed this shape and was partially
backfilled by #1804/PR#1809 -- but that backfill's own scope note
explicitly limited itself to the helper, leaving the caller open.

Two confirmed instances of the same shape, each empirically verified
by reverting the call site to its pre-fix behavior and confirming the
relevant test file(s) stay green, then restoring cleanly
(`git status --porcelain` clean afterward in both cases):

1. **#1691 (PR#1759): `checkPostMergeCleanupBacklog`'s trust-check call
   site.** `readCleanupEvidenceTrustedLogins` (`src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts`,
   around line 1960) itself has direct unit tests since #1804/PR#1809.
   Its only production caller, `checkPostMergeCleanupBacklog`
   (`src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts:1976`), builds the `hasTrustedEvidence`
   verdict at lines 2110-2124 by parsing `gh api .../comments` TSV
   output and checking each cleanup-evidence marker's author against
   `trustedLogins`. Reverting line 2123's `trustedLogins.has(login)`
   check to the pre-#1759 fail-open shape (`return login.length > 0`,
   i.e. "any non-empty login counts as trusted") and running the full
   suite (`pnpm test`, 3047 tests) leaves it green -- nothing exercises
   `checkPostMergeCleanupBacklog` itself with realistic `gh`-shaped
   comment data.
2. **#1686 (PR#1769): `collectFromGitHub`'s claim-evidence wiring.**
   `classifyClaimCandidateAmbiguity` and `hasTrustedClaimMarkerHistory`
   (`src/scripts/advisory-convergence.mts`) both have direct unit
   tests, and the verdict logic that consumes their *values*
   (`computeAdvisoryConvergenceVerdict`'s `indeterminate`-status
   handling) is itself thoroughly tested by directly constructing
   `AdvisoryConvergenceInputs` with `claimCandidateAmbiguous: true` /
   `claimMarkerHistoryPresent: true`. But the only place that actually
   *computes* those two fields from real claim-candidate data and
   forwards them into the verdict inputs is `collectFromGitHub`
   (private, line 1388; the call sites are lines 1523/1535, wired into
   the returned `inputs` object at lines 1599-1600) -- the real-GitHub
   I/O layer the CLI runs through via `defaultDeps.collect =
   collectFromGitHub` (line 1322). Dropping those two fields entirely
   from `collectFromGitHub`'s returned inputs (simulating the wiring
   never having been added) leaves the full
   `tests/advisory-convergence.test.mts` suite green (102/102 passing)
   -- with the fields silently defaulting to `false` inside
   `computeAdvisoryConvergenceVerdict`, an IDD-shaped PR with broken
   claim linkage falls back to `not_applicable`/`ready: true` instead
   of the intended `indeterminate`/`ready: false`, which is the exact
   fail-open #1686 exists to close. No test in this repository invokes
   `collectFromGitHub` (directly or via a stubbed-`gh` CLI run of
   `scripts/advisory-convergence.mjs`); `tests/advisory-convergence.test.mts`
   line 930's own comment documents that `collectFromGitHub` is
   deliberately "I/O layer, not under test here" for its
   longer-standing fields (e.g. `trustedMarkerLogins` resolution), so
   this gap is consistent with -- not a deviation from -- that existing
   convention; it is called out here because the two NEW #1686 fields
   are the ones whose omission is fail-open specifically, unlike that
   convention's other untested fields.

The other seven tracks (#1687, #1688, #1689, #1690, #1692, #1693,
#1694) were each checked the same way and found NOT to have this gap:
#1687's `evaluateResumeClaimRouting`/`evaluateFreshClaimGate`, #1688's
`classifyCiChecks`, and #1689's `summarizeRequiredChecks`/
`buildPreMergeReadinessSummary` are all exercised directly with
realistic inputs that hit the exact defensive branch; #1692 added a
CLI-level stubbed-`gh` smoke test
(`tests/gh-pagination-parsing-smoke.test.mts`) that runs the real
generated `scripts/*.mjs` end to end; #1693's three extractions each
carry both a direct unit test and an explicit "proven against the
actual wired ... function, not just the underlying helper" parity
test; #1690 and #1694 are prose/instructions-only changes with no
extracted code helper (phrase-assertion coverage already exists for
#1690 via #1804/PR#1809). No further follow-up is proposed for those
seven.

## Proposed change

Test-only backfill, no production behavior change, for the two call
sites above:

1. **`checkPostMergeCleanupBacklog` (`src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts`).**
   Add coverage that exercises the real function (not just
   `readCleanupEvidenceTrustedLogins` in isolation) with realistic
   `gh api .../comments` TSV-shaped output, covering: a trusted
   author's `idd-cleanup-evidence` marker suppresses the backlog
   warning; an untrusted author's identically-shaped marker does NOT
   suppress it (the regression this backfill locks in); and the
   existing `evidenceFailures` non-ok-fetch path is unaffected. Since
   `checkPostMergeCleanupBacklog` shells out via the module's private
   `runCommand`/`execFileSync('gh', ...)` (no injection seam), reuse
   the stubbed-`gh`-on-`PATH` CLI-smoke pattern
   `tests/gh-pagination-parsing-smoke.test.mts` (#1692) already
   established: invoke the real `scripts/idd-doctor.mjs` with
   `--require-github` against a temp git repo, with `gh` stubbed to
   return a merged-PR list and per-PR comment TSVs for both the
   trusted- and untrusted-author cases, and assert the resulting
   `--json` report's backlog warning presence/absence and the `missing`
   PR numbers it names.
2. **`collectFromGitHub`'s claim-evidence wiring
   (`src/scripts/advisory-convergence.mts`).** Add coverage that
   exercises the real wiring from raw claim-candidate comment data
   through to the `indeterminate` verdict -- not just
   `classifyClaimCandidateAmbiguity`/`hasTrustedClaimMarkerHistory` in
   isolation, and not just `computeAdvisoryConvergenceVerdict` with the
   two fields hand-supplied. Either of two approaches (pick whichever
   keeps the diff smaller):
   - Extend the same stubbed-`gh`-on-`PATH` CLI-smoke pattern to
     `scripts/advisory-convergence.mjs`, feeding it a stubbed multi-
     candidate claim-issue comment history that reproduces path 2
     (multiple resolving candidates) or path 4 (stale trusted claim,
     no active claim) from #1686's issue body, and asserting the CLI's
     JSON verdict reports `applicability.status: "indeterminate"` and
     `ready: false`; or
   - Export `collectFromGitHub` (or refactor it into an exported, pure
     sub-step that takes already-fetched `claimCandidates` and
     `trustedMarkerLogins` and returns the two fields, mirroring
     `filterResolvingClaimCandidates`'s existing shared-helper
     pattern), and add direct unit tests proving it wires
     `classifyClaimCandidateAmbiguity`/`hasTrustedClaimMarkerHistory`'s
     output into the same fields `computeAdvisoryConvergenceVerdict`
     already consumes.
3. If any `.mts` source changes (for example an `export` keyword, or a
   small extraction), run `pnpm run build` so the generated
   `scripts/*.mjs` mirrors stay byte-identical, per
   `docs/typescript-sources.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new test exercises `checkPostMergeCleanupBacklog` (not just
      `readCleanupEvidenceTrustedLogins`) end to end and would fail
      against the pre-#1759 fail-open shape (`return login.length >
      0`) at `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts`'s `hasTrustedEvidence` check.
- [ ] A new test exercises `collectFromGitHub`'s claim-evidence wiring
      (directly or via a stubbed-`gh` CLI run) and would fail if the
      `claimMarkerHistoryPresent`/`claimCandidateAmbiguous` computation
      or forwarding into `computeAdvisoryConvergenceVerdict`'s inputs
      were dropped.
- [ ] `pnpm test` passes with the new tests included.
- [ ] `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` passes with no new drift.
- [ ] No runtime behavior changes: this issue only adds regression-test
      coverage for fixes that already merged in PR#1759 (#1691) and
      PR#1769 (#1686), plus any purely visibility/extraction changes
      needed to make the real call site directly testable.

Refs: #1712, #1691, #1759, #1686, #1769, #1804, #1809
